Thought: I need to determine what characteristic feature a compound must have to be classified as a conjugated diene.

A conjugated diene is a compound that contains two carbon-carbon double bonds (C=C) separated by one single bond. This arrangement allows for the overlap of p-orbitals across all four carbon atoms, creating a conjugated system. The key feature is the conjugation of the double bonds, which means they are separated by exactly one single bond, allowing for electron delocalization.

Looking at the options:
A. Two aromatic rings - This is not the definition of a conjugated diene. Aromatic rings have cyclic conjugated systems, but a conjugated diene specifically refers to two C=C bonds in conjugation.
B. Two carbonyl groups - Carbonyl groups (C=O) are not related to the definition of a conjugated diene.
C. Two conjugated C=C bonds - This correctly describes a conjugated diene, which has two C=C bonds that are conjugated (separated by one single bond).
D. Two hydroxyl groups - Hydroxyl groups (-OH) are not related to the definition of a conjugated diene.

The correct answer is C. Two conjugated C=C bonds.
